assessment: The adoptive transfer of NK cells expressing chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) has generated significant interest for cancer immunotherapy, considering recent success of CAR-NK cells in treating B cell malignancies with fewer deleterious side effects, as compared to CAR-T cell therapies. In this paper, the authors engineered NK cells expressing a CAR targeting CD73, which is highly expressed in lung adenocarcinomas and generates immunosuppressive adenosine. Their CD73.CAR-NK cells not only exhibited improved infiltration of and enhanced cytotoxicity toward CD73-expressing tumor cells, but also significantly reduced adenosine production by a lung adenocarcinoma line, which has potential to further improve anti-tumor immune responses.
